title: Ataxia telangiectasia mutated kinase regulates hydroquinone-induced hepatic redox and iron Dyshomeostasis via the NRF2-GPX4 Signaling pathway
content:
Abstract
Hydroquinone (HQ), a primary toxic metabolite of benzene, is known to induce oxidative stress and disrupt iron metabolism, yet the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Ataxia Telangiectasia Mutated Kinase (ATM) has recently been implicated in redox signaling and iron homeostasis. Given the critical role of the Nuclear Factor Erythroid 2-Related Factor 2 (NRF2)-Glutathione Peroxidase 4 (GPX4) pathway in antioxidant defense and ferroptosis inhibition, this study aimed to investigate whether ATM regulates HQ-induced redox and iron imbalances via this pathway. Results showed a dose-dependent biphasic pattern of HQ in vivo: low-dose HQ (12.5 mg/kg) induced systemic oxidative stress and hepatic iron accumulation, whereas high-dose HQ (50 mg/kg) activated hepatic antioxidant defenses (upregulated NRF2 and GPX4), upregulated ferritin for iron sequestration, and reduced available iron levels. Mechanistically, phosphorylated ATM (p-ATM) increased at 25 mg/kg HQ but decreased at 50 mg/kg, indicating dose-dependent inhibition of ATM activity in vivo. ATM inhibition reversed HQ-induced toxic effects by restoring GPX4 and Ferritin Heavy Chain 1 (FTH1) expression, reducing total iron accumulation and lipid peroxidation, and increasing Glutathione levels, despite elevated Reactive Oxygen Species levels in HL-7702 cells. These findings are consistent with ATM modulating HQ-induced hepatic redox and iron homeostasis imbalance, potentially through the NRF2-GPX4 pathway, and suggest that ATM may be a candidate target for mitigating benzene/HQ-induced toxicity.
